entries.name: setup
entries.summary: Runs once when the board starts or resets. Put pinMode(), Serial.begin() and other start-up code here.

entries.name: loop
entries.summary: Runs over and over after setup() finishes, for as long as the board has power. This is where your program does its work.

entries.name: if
entries.summary: Runs a block of code only when the condition is true; the optional else block runs when it's false. Compare with ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=.
entries.note: Use == to compare. A single = sets a value, so if (x = 5) is always true.

entries.name: for
entries.summary: Repeats a block a set number of times, usually counting with a variable.

entries.name: while
entries.summary: Repeats a block as long as the condition stays true. Make sure something inside changes the condition, or it never stops.

entries.name: pinMode
entries.summary: Sets a pin to work as an input or an output. Call it in setup() for every pin you use.
params: the GPIO number, for example 2 or LED_BUILTIN
entries.example:
pinMode(LED_BUILTIN, OUTPUT);
pinMode(0, INPUT_PULLUP);  // button to GND

entries.name: digitalWrite
entries.summary: Turns an output pin on (HIGH, 3.3 V) or off (LOW, 0 V). The pin must be set to OUTPUT with pinMode() first.
entries.note: On most ESP8266 boards the built-in LED is wired the other way round: LOW turns it on.

entries.name: digitalRead
entries.summary: Reads whether an input pin is HIGH or LOW.
entries.note: With INPUT_PULLUP, a button wired to GND reads LOW when pressed.

entries.name: analogRead
entries.summary: Measures the voltage on an analog pin and returns it as a number.
params: an analog-capable pin, for example 34 on the ESP32 or A0 on the ESP8266
entries.returns: 0 to 4095 on the ESP32 (0–3.3 V), 0 to 1023 on the ESP8266
entries.note: On the ESP32, pins of ADC2 (e.g. 0, 2, 4, 12–15, 25–27) can't be read while Wi-Fi is on. Use ADC1 pins 32–39.

entries.name: analogWrite
entries.summary: Outputs a PWM signal, which looks like a voltage between 0 and 3.3 V to an LED or motor. Use it to dim LEDs or set speeds.

entries.name: analogReadResolution
entries.summary: Sets how many bits analogRead() returns (9–12 on the ESP32). 12 bits gives 0–4095.

entries.name: delay
entries.summary: Pauses the program for the given number of milliseconds (1000 ms = 1 second). Nothing else in loop() runs while it waits.
params: how long to wait, in milliseconds
entries.note: To do several things at once, use millis() instead (see the BlinkWithoutDelay example).

entries.name: delayMicroseconds
entries.summary: Pauses for the given number of microseconds (1,000,000 µs = 1 second). For very short, precise waits.
params: how long to wait, in microseconds

entries.name: millis
entries.summary: Returns how many milliseconds have passed since the board started. Use it to time things without stopping the program.

entries.name: micros
entries.summary: Returns how many microseconds have passed since the board started.

entries.name: map
entries.summary: Re-scales a number from one range to another, for example a 0–4095 sensor reading to 0–100 %.

entries.name: constrain
entries.summary: Keeps a number inside a range: returns low if x is smaller, high if x is bigger, otherwise x.

entries.name: random
entries.summary: Returns a random whole number from min (default 0) up to but not including max.

entries.name: abs
entries.summary: Returns the value without its sign: abs(-5) is 5.

entries.name: min
entries.summary: Returns the smaller of two numbers.

entries.name: max
entries.summary: Returns the bigger of two numbers.

entries.name: Serial.begin
entries.summary: Starts the serial connection so the board can send text to the Serial Monitor. Call it once in setup().
params: baud rate; 115200 is standard for ESP boards. The Serial Monitor must use the same speed.

entries.name: Serial.print
entries.summary: Sends text or a number to the Serial Monitor without starting a new line.

entries.name: Serial.println
entries.summary: Sends text or a number to the Serial Monitor, then starts a new line.

entries.name: Serial.printf
entries.summary: Prints formatted text on ESP boards: %d for whole numbers, %f for decimals, %s for text.

entries.name: Serial.available
entries.summary: Returns how many characters have arrived from the Serial Monitor and are waiting to be read.
entries.returns: number of bytes waiting (0 if none)

entries.name: Serial.read
entries.summary: Reads one character sent from the Serial Monitor.
entries.returns: the character, or -1 if nothing is waiting

entries.name: Serial.readStringUntil
entries.summary: Reads text from the Serial Monitor up to a character, usually the new line '\n'.

entries.name: tone
entries.syntax: tone(pin, frequency)  or  tone(pin, frequency, ms)
entries.summary: Plays a square-wave sound on a pin, for a buzzer or small speaker.
params: pitch in Hz, e.g. 440 for the note A
entries.example: tone(25, 440, 500);  // A for half a second

entries.name: noTone
entries.summary: Stops a sound started with tone().

entries.name: pulseIn
entries.summary: Measures how long a pin stays HIGH (or LOW), in microseconds. Used with ultrasonic distance sensors.
entries.returns: pulse length in microseconds (0 on timeout)
entries.example:
long us = pulseIn(ECHO, HIGH);
float cm = us / 58.0;

entries.name: attachInterrupt
entries.summary: Runs a function immediately when a pin changes, even in the middle of loop().
params: a short function with no parameters
entries.note: Keep the function short. On ESP boards mark it IRAM_ATTR, and make shared variables volatile.

entries.name: HIGH
entries.summary: The two digital levels: HIGH is on (3.3 V on ESP boards), LOW is off (0 V). Used with digitalWrite() and digitalRead().

entries.name: OUTPUT
entries.summary: Pin modes for pinMode(). OUTPUT drives a pin. INPUT reads it. INPUT_PULLUP reads it with a built-in resistor to 3.3 V, so a button to GND reads LOW when pressed and no external resistor is needed.

entries.name: LED_BUILTIN
entries.summary: The pin number of the board's built-in LED, so sketches work on different boards. It's GPIO 2 on most ESP32 dev boards.
entries.note: Some ESP32 boards don't define it; the Blink example adds #define LED_BUILTIN 2 if it's missing.

entries.name: String
entries.summary: Holds text. You can join Strings with +, and get the length with .length().

entries.name: WiFi.begin
entries.summary: Starts connecting to a Wi-Fi network. Connecting takes a few seconds, so wait until WiFi.status() is WL_CONNECTED.
entries.note: #include <WiFi.h> on the ESP32 or #include <ESP8266WiFi.h> on the ESP8266. Most boards only use 2.4 GHz networks.

entries.name: WiFi.status
entries.summary: Returns the connection state. WL_CONNECTED means you're connected.

entries.name: WiFi.localIP
entries.summary: Returns the board's IP address once connected, so you can reach a web server running on it.

entries.name: WiFi.softAP
entries.summary: Makes the board its own Wi-Fi hotspot that phones can join. The password needs at least 8 characters.

entries.name: WiFi.scanNetworks
entries.summary: Looks for nearby Wi-Fi networks. Afterwards WiFi.SSID(i) and WiFi.RSSI(i) give each one's name and signal strength.

entries.name: ledcAttach
entries.summary: Sets up a pin for ESP32 PWM (LED control). Afterwards ledcWrite() sets its brightness.

entries.name: ledcWrite
entries.summary: Sets the PWM duty on a pin set up with ledcAttach(): 0 is off, the maximum (255 at 8 bits) is fully on.

entries.name: touchRead
entries.summary: Reads an ESP32 touch pin. The number gets smaller when a finger touches the wire or pad.

entries.name: esp_deep_sleep_start
entries.summary: Puts the ESP32 into deep sleep to save power. It wakes by restarting, so the sketch starts again from setup().

entries.name: ESP.deepSleep
entries.summary: Puts the ESP8266 into deep sleep. Connect GPIO16 (D0) to RST so the timer can wake it; it restarts from setup().

entries.name: ESP.restart
entries.summary: Restarts the board, like pressing its reset button.
